test: one-sided exact binomial test H0: p <= baseline; BROKEN iff p_value < alpha; interval: Wilson score on p, mapped to advantage
caveat: This is falsification evidence, not a proof. Each cell runs a fixed, finite set of concrete attack strategies against deliberately broken toy components for a finite number of seeded trials. BROKEN means an implemented attack won significantly more often than chance (a concrete, reproducible attack). NO ATTACK FOUND means only that the implemented strategies did not; it is not a security statement, says nothing about attacks not implemented here (in particular generic or cryptanalytic attacks on ML-KEM, HQC, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, Ed25519 or SHA3, quantum attacks, side channels, multi-user settings, and key-reuse settings beyond the one stripping game), and the failure models are idealised: a real component that fails will fail in its own way. The results complement, and do not replace, the cited GHP18 theorem and the unreviewed proof sketches in docs/SECURITY.md.
